question: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.

raiseTranscript.text: My manager said I asked good clarifying questions early so I didn't block others. I still missed one edge case but fixed it the next day after the review.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: New grad converting to full-time on backend team
Situation: Forced language switch + new codebase in 2 weeks
Actions: Paired, took notes on reviews, asked clarifying questions early
Outcome: Owned small fix with 8% latency win; manager noted good questions
Quote: "I still missed one edge case but fixed it the next day"
Follow-up: What feedback did you get? -> Showed coachability and quick iteration
junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows quick ramp on new language and codebase through pairing and note-taking, with concrete outcome of owning a fix. Quote about fixing the edge case the next day demonstrates learning from feedback. Biggest strength is proactive clarification that prevented blocking others.

lowerTranscript.text: Did you ask anyone for help?
Not really, I didn't want to bother people. I just read docs until I caught up.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: New grad on first team switch
Situation: New stack, tried solo for a month
Actions: Read docs, avoided asking questions
Outcome: Stayed stuck on basics, no visible progress mentioned
Quote: "I didn't want to bother people"
Follow-up: Did you ask anyone for help? -> Avoided collaboration
junior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for junior. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows isolation for a full month with no progress metric or help-seeking. Quote reveals reluctance to ask questions. Biggest gap is lack of coachability and ownership of own learning speed.

raiseTranscript.text: The integration shipped two weeks early and reduced manual reconciliation by 40%. I also wrote a short onboarding guide that the team still uses.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: Senior engineer joining payments from ads
Situation: New domain + cross-team integration deadline
Actions: 1:1s with partners, mapped APIs in shared doc, created onboarding guide
Outcome: Shipped early, 40% reduction in manual work
Quote: "The integration shipped two weeks early"
Follow-up: What was the measurable impact? -> Clear metrics and lasting artifact
senior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for senior. Competency: Adaptability. Story demonstrates cross-team influence and domain ramp while delivering ahead of schedule. Quote about early ship and 40% reduction ties directly to impact. Biggest strength is creating reusable documentation that helps others adapt too.

lowerTranscript.text: How did you adjust your approach?
I stopped pushing after a couple of meetings. It took longer but I didn't want to make waves.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: Senior joining new company
Situation: Shift from fast to consensus culture
Actions: Pushed initially then stopped advocating
Outcome: Slowed down with no personal adjustment described
Quote: "I stopped pushing after a couple of meetings"
Follow-up: How did you adjust your approach? -> Passive withdrawal
senior.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for senior. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows failure to adapt influence style, resulting in disengagement. Quote reveals retreat rather than finding new ways to drive progress. Biggest gap is lack of cross-team impact or proactive bridging.

raiseTranscript.text: How did the team perform after?
Within six weeks velocity stabilized and two engineers who had been looking to leave stayed. I also promoted one person who stepped up during the transition.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: Manager inheriting reorg team
Situation: Low morale, domain gap, retention risk
Actions: Listening tour, expert pairing, smaller-win planning
Outcome: Velocity stabilized, two retentions, one promotion
Quote: "Two engineers who had been looking to leave stayed"
Follow-up: How did the team perform after? -> Team-level outcomes and development
manager.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for manager. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows building team leverage through structured onboarding and adjusted planning. Quote about retentions and promotion links directly to people development. Biggest strength is owning team outcomes instead of individual heroics.

lowerTranscript.text: They stayed flat. I didn't have the bandwidth to change everything at once.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: New manager of existing team
Situation: Process mismatch with prior experience
Actions: Tried old playbook then disengaged
Outcome: Results stayed flat, no team development
Quote: "I didn't have the bandwidth to change everything"
Follow-up: What happened to team results? -> No ownership of outcomes
manager.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for manager. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows retreat from team leadership when adaptation proved difficult. Quote about bandwidth reveals abdication. Biggest gap is absence of any people development or leverage creation.

raiseTranscript.text: We retained 92% of the acquired talent and hit the combined roadmap targets two months early. The playbook became the template for two later acquisitions.

raiseNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: Exec leading post-acquisition integration
Situation: 80 engineers, cultural clash, velocity risk
Actions: Joint steering group, 90-day playbook, personal office hours
Outcome: 92% retention, roadmap hit early, reusable template
Quote: "The playbook became the template for two later acquisitions"
Follow-up: What was the business result? -> Org-level metrics and strategic reuse
exec.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for exec. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows strategic judgment on structure and long-term leverage through reusable playbook. Quote about 92% retention and early roadmap delivery ties to business impact. Biggest strength is turning one integration into an org capability.

lowerTranscript.text: Some friction lingered for months and a few key people left. We still hit the quarterly numbers but it was harder than expected.

lowerNotes: Q: Tell me about a time you moved to a new team, role, company, or culture and had to adapt quickly.
Role: Exec after reorg
Situation: Conflicting priorities across teams
Actions: Issued org chart and goals, skipped cultural work
Outcome: Friction persisted, key attrition, harder execution
Quote: "Some friction lingered for months"
Follow-up: How did the teams respond? -> Long-term cost of shallow adaptation
exec.lowerFeedback: Lowers the bar for exec. Competency: Adaptability. Story shows focus on structure over culture, producing sustained friction and attrition. Quote about lingering friction reveals underestimation of long-term costs. Biggest gap is absence of strategic trade-off thinking or org-level leverage.

diagnostic.manager: Listening tour + pairing for whole team

diagnostic.senior: Shared doc and 1:1s with other teams
diagnostic.exec: Joint steering group across acquired org
